neighbours.label: the first split piece (' min', ' tr', ' ban') of minuscule, trite, trifle and banal: words that play something down as tiny or trivial
fire: Next to the national debt, that sum is truly minuscule.
Critics found the plot trite and the songs forgettable.
The whole argument began over a mere trifle at dinner.
Most of what he said on stage was utterly banal.
Against such huge forces, our efforts were minuscule indeed.
Her poems about love felt trite to the younger readers.
He pays no attention to such a trifle as money.
The small talk at these parties is always so banal.
quiet: Measured against the national debt, this figure looks truly enormous.
Readers called the plot gripping and the songs memorable.
A heated argument broke out over the large bill at dinner.
Nearly everything she said on stage was deeply moving.
Facing such huge forces, our army's courage was remarkable indeed.
Younger readers found his poems about love quite thrilling.
He pays careful attention to subjects such as money.
Conversation at these dinners is always so lively.

notes: Second round. The first round used a wider set (negligible, petty, paltry, mundane) and shared prefixes with its near misses; it failed at AUROC 0.891 because 'this cost is enormous' fired 0.456 on the shared ' is', and whole-token synonyms stayed low. New probes: ' tr' in trifle 0.571 and trite 0.474, ' ban' 0.426, ' min' 0.368 and 0.109; 'trivial' 0.058, 'trial' 0.001, 'bank' 0.001, 'minister' 0.002. Narrower label, split pieces only, and near misses that keep the topics with different lead-ins and no shared prefix. Tokens are checked for every fire sentence.
